provenance: Hand-authored synthetic scenarios. Expected rule labels describe which activity an analyst should review, using the scenario context. Not independent or representative of production traffic.
unit: One case × one rule label; multiple alerts with the same rule in a case count once.

cases.name: A corrected password
cases.note: Two mistakes followed by success; below the review threshold.

cases.name: Failures followed by success
cases.note: Investigate the successful session; compromise is not assumed.

cases.name: Multiple accounts from one source
cases.note: Five distinct accounts in a short period.

cases.name: Mixed repeated failures and success
cases.note: Two different rule labels are expected.

cases.name: Separate sources, unrelated accounts
cases.note: Events must not be merged into a spray from one source.

cases.name: Successful session from a different source
cases.note: Success correlation requires the same source and account.

cases.name: Known benign maintenance retries
cases.note: Intentional false-positive example: maintenance context is known to the labeler but absent from the logs.

cases.name: Slow attempts requiring review
cases.note: Intentional miss: the labelled suspicious sequence is too slow for the current five-minute rule.

cases.name: Failures spanning midnight
cases.note: UTC dates must be retained when events cross midnight.

cases.name: IPv6 source
cases.note: IPv6 is handled the same way as IPv4.
